claims.text: Local lattice distortion governs superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys.
Electronic disorder governs superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys.
HRTEM and neutron scattering can reveal the relevant local lattice distortion.
HRTEM and neutron scattering can reveal the relevant electronic disorder.
Systematic variation of alloy composition can control local lattice distortion and electronic disorder.
Systematic variation of processing conditions can control local lattice distortion and electronic disorder.
Variation in local lattice distortion influences the superconducting order parameter.
Variation in electronic disorder influences the superconducting order parameter.
Greater local lattice distortion will reduce the superconducting critical temperature.
Greater electronic disorder will reduce the superconducting critical temperature.
Greater local lattice distortion will increase the pressure sensitivity of superconductivity.
Greater electronic disorder will increase the pressure sensitivity of superconductivity.
High-entropy alloys with minimal lattice distortion and electronic disorder exhibit robust zero-resistance superconductivity.
The hypothesis applies to high-entropy alloys in the dirty limit.
In the dirty limit, the electron mean free path is shorter than the superconducting coherence length.
The relevant tests are to be performed at low temperature and high pressure.
The exact relationship among lattice distortion, electronic disorder, and superconducting behavior is not well understood.
Finding no correlation between lattice distortion or electronic disorder and superconducting behavior would falsify the hypothesis.
